title: Les êtres vivants autour de nous
oneGoal: Students will identify and distinguish between living and non-living things in their environment
decisionPoints: What living and non-living examples can students easily observe in our classroom?
Should we start with plants, animals, or a mix of both living things?
Are students ready for simple living vs non-living sorting activities?
progression: Foundation lesson - establishes core understanding of what makes something alive before exploring specific needs
realWorldConnection: Understanding the difference between living pets, plants, and toys or furniture at home

title: De quoi ont besoin les plantes pour vivre?
oneGoal: Students will identify that plants need water, sunlight, and air to stay alive and healthy
decisionPoints: Which plant needs are most visible to students in our classroom?
Should we use real plants or pictures to demonstrate plant needs?
Are students ready for simple plant care activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by exploring specific needs of living plants through observation and care
realWorldConnection: Understanding why parents water house plants and put them near windows

title: Expérience: les plantes et l'eau
oneGoal: Students will conduct a simple experiment to observe how plants react when they have or don't have water
decisionPoints: What type of plants work best for classroom water experiments?
Should we use two plants or one plant with two sections?
Are students ready for prediction-making before experiments?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by testing plant water needs through hands-on experimentation
realWorldConnection: Learning why gardens need watering and what happens when plants don't get enough water

title: Les plantes ont besoin de lumière
oneGoal: Students will understand that plants need light to grow and will observe what happens without sunlight
decisionPoints: How can we safely demonstrate light needs without harming classroom plants?
Should we use natural sunlight or artificial light for demonstrations?
Are students ready for comparing plants in different light conditions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by exploring light requirements through observation and simple experiments
realWorldConnection: Understanding why plants lean toward windows and why they grow better outside

title: De quoi ont besoin les animaux pour vivre?
oneGoal: Students will identify that animals need food, water, air, and shelter to stay alive and healthy
decisionPoints: Which animal examples are most familiar to students (pets, wild animals, insects)?
Should we focus on one type of animal or compare different animals?
Are students ready for comparing animal and plant needs?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by exploring animal needs and comparing them to plant requirements
realWorldConnection: Understanding why pets need food bowls, water dishes, and safe places to sleep

title: Les bébés animaux grandissent
oneGoal: Students will observe that baby animals grow into adult animals and need special care when young
decisionPoints: Which baby animal examples are most engaging for Grade 1 students?
Should we use real photos, books, or videos to show animal growth?
Are students ready for sequencing animal growth stages?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by exploring animal growth patterns and development needs
realWorldConnection: Connecting to students' own growth and observing how pets or farm animals change

title: Comment prendre soin d'une plante?
oneGoal: Students will learn practical ways to care for plants by providing water, light, and proper conditions
decisionPoints: What type of classroom plant is easiest for students to care for successfully?
Should each student have their own plant or should we share class plants?
Are students ready for daily plant care responsibilities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by applying knowledge of plant needs through hands-on care activities
realWorldConnection: Learning responsibility by helping care for plants at home or in the garden

title: Comment aider les animaux?
oneGoal: Students will identify ways to help animals by providing food, water, and safe spaces
decisionPoints: Which animals can students safely help (birds, insects, classroom pets)?
Should we focus on wild animals or pets for helping activities?
Are students ready for discussions about animal safety and boundaries?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by extending care concepts to animals and exploring helping behaviors
realWorldConnection: Understanding how to safely help birds, pets, and other animals in their community

title: Notre jardin de classe
oneGoal: Students will plant seeds and create a classroom garden to observe plant growth and practice care
decisionPoints: What seeds are most likely to grow successfully in our classroom conditions?
Should we plant in individual pots or create a shared class garden?
Are students ready for long-term plant observation activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by creating a living laboratory for ongoing plant care and observation
realWorldConnection: Learning where food comes from and how gardens help provide for living things

title: Observer la croissance de nos plantes
oneGoal: Students will measure and record plant growth over time using simple tools and observations
decisionPoints: What measurement tools are appropriate for Grade 1 students?
Should we measure height, count leaves, or observe other growth signs?
Are students ready for creating simple growth charts?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by developing scientific observation and recording skills through plant monitoring
realWorldConnection: Understanding how scientists track changes in living things over time

title: Les humains ont des besoins aussi
oneGoal: Students will identify human needs (food, water, air, shelter) and compare them to plant and animal needs
decisionPoints: Which human needs are most obvious to students in their daily lives?
Should we focus on basic survival needs or include comfort needs?
Are students ready for three-way comparisons (plants, animals, humans)?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by connecting living thing needs to students' own experiences and needs
realWorldConnection: Understanding why families provide food, water, homes, and fresh air for health

title: Créer un habitat pour les petites créatures
oneGoal: Students will design and create a simple habitat that provides what small creatures need to survive
decisionPoints: Which small creatures are appropriate for classroom habitat creation?
Should we focus on insects, worms, or other small animals?
Are students ready for habitat design thinking and planning?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by applying understanding of living thing needs to create supportive environments
realWorldConnection: Understanding how gardens, parks, and natural areas provide what animals need

title: Nos plantes après plusieurs semaines
oneGoal: Students will evaluate their plant care success and identify what helped or hindered plant growth
decisionPoints: How can students assess plant health and growth objectively?
Should we compare different student plants or focus on individual progress?
Are students ready for problem-solving discussions about plant care?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by reflecting on care practices and evaluating outcomes of plant experiments
realWorldConnection: Learning from gardening experiences and understanding what makes plants thrive

title: Célébrer les êtres vivants
oneGoal: Students will create a class presentation showing what they learned about caring for living things
decisionPoints: What format best showcases student learning about living things?
Should presentations focus on plants, animals, or both?
Are students ready for sharing their care experiences with others?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by synthesizing learning and communicating discoveries about living things
realWorldConnection: Sharing knowledge about caring for living things with family and community

title: Les saisons et les besoins des vivants
oneGoal: Students will explore how the needs of living things change with different seasons (extension)
decisionPoints: Which seasonal changes in living thing needs are most visible to students?
Should we focus on plants, animals, or both for seasonal adaptations?
Are students ready for cause-and-effect discussions about seasons?
progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - applies living thing knowledge to seasonal variations and adaptations
realWorldConnection: Understanding why gardens change seasonally and animals behave differently in winter

title: Protéger les habitats
oneGoal: Students will identify ways humans can protect natural habitats that living things need (extension)
decisionPoints: Which habitat protection concepts are appropriate for Grade 1 understanding?
Should we focus on local habitats or include broader environmental concepts?
Are students ready for action-planning discussions about habitat protection?
progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - expands caring concepts to environmental stewardship and conservation
realWorldConnection: Understanding how families can help protect parks, forests, and natural areas

title: Les êtres vivants qui nous aident
oneGoal: Students will explore how different living things help humans and other living things survive (extension)
decisionPoints: Which examples of helpful living things are most concrete for students?
Should we focus on plants that help, animals that help, or both?
Are students ready for interdependence concepts in simple terms?
progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - explores mutual relationships and how living things support each other
realWorldConnection: Understanding how bees help flowers, trees help clean air, and pets help families

title: Devenir des experts en soins
oneGoal: Students will teach younger students or family members about caring for living things (extension)
decisionPoints: What teaching format works best for Grade 1 students to share knowledge?
Should students teach about plants, animals, or choose their own focus?
Are students ready for peer teaching responsibilities?
progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - consolidates learning through teaching others and sharing expertise
realWorldConnection: Building confidence by teaching family members about plant and animal care

title: Notre livre des êtres vivants
oneGoal: Students will create a class book documenting all their discoveries about living things and their care (extension)
decisionPoints: What book format best showcases the range of student learning?
Should the book include photos, drawings, or written observations?
Are students ready for collaborative book creation activities?
progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - creates lasting documentation of scientific learning and discoveries
realWorldConnection: Creating a resource that families can use to continue caring for living things at home

title: Fête des petits gardiens de la vie
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their learning journey by showcasing their plant care success and animal knowledge (extension)
decisionPoints: How can the celebration highlight each student's growth in caring for living things?
Should we include live plants, habitat displays, or both in the celebration?
What activities best demonstrate student learning to families?
progression: Extension of Lesson 19 - celebrates the complete unit while building community connections and scientific confidence
realWorldConnection: Sharing our success in caring for living things with families and building ongoing commitment to environmental care
